title: C1 - Chat, mission pipeline, and progress
outcome: The console has a chat surface wired to the existing chat pipeline, with a normal mode carrying a model picker and a Domain-Capabilities mode carrying the delivery workspace. The four-stage mission pipeline runs as a tooling-level bench against granted missions: plan by Claude at Opus 5 or above, develop and commit by the local model in an isolated worktree, a bounded review loop by Codex, and final review, approval and merge by Claude at Opus 5 or above, under machine accounts with auto-merge armed and the definition of done checked mechanically. A session status feed in the draft job-protocol-v2 shape drives a read-only progress panel, and the coordinator answers what needs the Person from pending-decision state. When a plan proves unclean the mission escalates through the existing user-decision functionality and waits.
notInScope: No broker or store change - that is MS-0002. The bench implementation is disposable by declaration under D7: it retires when MS-0002 and MS-0003 land, and only the status feed format survives. No new coordinator provider - that is MS-0015. The local model is assigned the smallest mechanical issues first; its weakness relative to the other two workers is a stated operating constraint, not a discovery to be made in review.
completionEvidence: A granted rehearsal mission runs the full pipeline unattended on a real issue: the plan is recorded, the local model commits under its machine account, the review loop completes at least one correction round, the acceptance role approves, auto-merge fires on the approval, and the evidence pack exists. A deliberately unclean plan escalates through the decision endpoint and resumes on the Person's decision, asserted by a test. A clean security-review-labelled rehearsal issue merges without escalation, while an injected security finding escalates and waits for the Founder; both paths are recorded in the evidence pack. The progress panel renders live sessions from the feed. The full suite is green throughout. On issues labelled security-review the acceptance stage performs the security review itself and escalates to the Founder only on a finding, never on the label alone; a mission touching schemas/canonical/ still escalates per D9.

metadata.origin: Folded in at the D7 rescope of 2026-08-20; the pipeline shape follows D8, the machine accounts D9.
metadata.risk: The bench executes model-driven subprocesses that commit and push under repository credentials - the riskiest surface in the milestone and the reason it carries a security review. The second risk is quiet scope growth: a bench that starts hosting features becomes the second dispatch path D7 forbids; the feed format is the only durable artifact.
